body.statement: There exist universal constants \(0<c<C<\infty\) such that for every sequence with \(d_n\to\infty\), \(d_n=o(\sqrt n)\), and \(nd_n\) even, \[\Pr_{G_n}\!\left\{c\,r_{\log}(n,d_n)\le R_2(G_n)\le C\,r_{\log}(n,d_n)\right\}\longrightarrow1.\] On the same graph event, the design-estimator returned by \(\mathsf{Compile}(G_n)\) has worst-case design MSE at most \(C\,r_{\log}(n,d_n)\) over exactly \(\mathcal M(G_n,\tau_{\mathrm{GATE}},2)\).
body.justification: This remains the desired field-tier closure of the exact unrestricted Kandiros--Harshaw--S\'{a}vje game, with an explicit risk scale and a total attaining procedure.
body.gap: All post-certificate implications are proved, but the dense full right-projected Boolean operator event remains open. The completed truncation step does not by itself close the upper edge, so the logarithmic minimax bracket is still unmatched.
body.consumer: A future proof would determine whether the deployed cluster-randomized \(d_n^2/n\) benchmark can be improved to \(d_n^2/[n\log(d_n+1)]\) in the declared random-regular benchmark.

obligation.what_is_open: The unconditional high-probability upper edge, and hence the matched frontier, remains open because the dense-range event \(\|B_{G_n}P_n\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le Ld_n^{7/4}\) has not been established.
obligation.obstruction: The established all-procedure converse, seed-risk theorem, and finite compiler close every statistical implication after the graph event, but none proves that event. The newly proved truncation estimate reduces the dense task to the grouped truncated polynomial, yet the proposed Xu instantiation loses the required signed cancellations, violates its stated trace-order premise, and controls only a sandwiched projection. Treating any of those missing bounds as a hypothesis would assume the kernel; restricting to the already proved sparse range would not answer the stated all-sequence problem.
obligation.attempted: I combined the established converse, seed upper bound, minimax definition, and compiler and verified that the compiler eventually chooses the seed procedure on the desired graph event. I also completed the dense Boolean truncation step. The only remaining failure is the dense full right-projected graph certificate, now split into a grouped Charlier trace bound and a row-sum fluctuation bound.
obligation.partial_result:
All implications after the missing dense graph certificate remain valid.  Let
\[
H_n=\{\|B_{G_n}P_n\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le Ld_n^{7/4}\}.
\]
The assumptions \(d_n=o(\sqrt n)\) and \(d_n\to\infty\) imply
\[
r_{\log}(n,d_n)
=\frac{d_n^2/n}{\log(d_n+1)}\longrightarrow0.
\tag{8}
\]
On \(H_n\), \(\mathrm{thm{:}seed\mbox{-}upper}\) bounds the exact worst-case seed-procedure risk by \(C_0r_{\log}(n,d_n)\).  By (8), this certificate is eventually below one, so \(\mathrm{def{:}finite\mbox{-}compiler}\) selects the seed law there; \(\mathrm{prop{:}finite\mbox{-}compiler}\) makes the selected rule a terminating observed-data procedure.  Therefore \(\mathrm{def{:}minimax\mbox{-}risk}\) gives
\[
R_2(G_n)\le C_0r_{\log}(n,d_n)\qquad\text{on }H_n.
\tag{9}
\]
Independently, \(\mathrm{thm{:}balanced\mbox{-}all\mbox{-}procedure\mbox{-}converse}\) gives events \(L_n\) with \(\Pr_{G_n}(L_n)\to1\) and
\[
R_2(G_n)\ge c_0r_{\log}(n,d_n)\qquad\text{on }L_n.
\tag{10}
\]
Thus (9)--(10) prove the advertised conclusion conditionally on \(\Pr_{G_n}(H_n)\to1\).  Equations (1)--(6) establish the Boolean-polynomial truncation needed on the dense subrange, but the grouped operator and row-sum estimates identified in (7) remain unavailable.  Consequently the frozen primitives do not establish \(\Pr_{G_n}(H_n)\to1\), and the unconditional matched frontier cannot yet be asserted.
